In West Chilliwack, the 55+ homes you can buy are Cottonwood Village (manufactured-home park). This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Cottonwood Village (Cottonwood Mobile Home Park) — 7610 Evans Road

Age-restricted 55+ manufactured-home park: 143 units, clubhouse, 1 pet allowed, on First Nations leased land. Current listing information for homes in the park states a lease expiry in 2076 with an option to extend, describes the park as a well-maintained 55+ community, and records "No strata" with a monthly pad fee — the buyer purchases the manufactured home and rents the pad; the land is not owned. Listing-stated lease detail — confirm against the park's lease and tenancy documents before relying on it.
Streets, schools and getting around West Chilliwack

items.t: The ground it covers is the western rural and agricultural part of the city, which the City plans through its Agricultural Area Plan, a schedule of the Official Community Plan; the plan states the farm sector there is dominated by dairy and poultry operations, nurseries and greenhouses.

The named corridor inside the area is Evans Road: Evans Elementary (K–5) is at 7600 Evans Road, and BC Transit route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Rd at Yale Rd, Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd and Downtown Chilliwack.

SD33 catchments are address-based: the locator result for the sample address 7600 Evans Road is Evans Elementary → Vedder Middle → Sardis Secondary (locator note: all students attending Vedder Middle must attend Sardis Secondary). Catchments for other addresses: run the specific address in the locator.
Highway 1 serves the north side of Chilliwack; interchange detail for this area is UNVERIFIED on the sources read.

The nearest City recreation centres are outside the area — Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, Unit 1, 9145 Corbould Street, and Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way — and the nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue.
One health service IS inside the corridor: the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #104 - 7955 Evans Road, co-located at the Chilliwack and Fraser Health Rural Primary Care Centre.

Where 55+ housing actually sits in Chilliwack: the Evans Road corridor holds the area's one verified 55+ product (a manufactured-home park); the city's 55+ strata condos and townhomes sit in Downtown Chilliwack, Sardis and Vedder Crossing, and its care residences sit on the east/downtown side —.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in West Chilliwack

items.t: Manufactured-home parks run on a different statute: pad tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act (MHPTA), not the Strata Property Act. A home owner must provide a purchaser with the written tenancy agreement and the written park rules, and a sale is an assignment of the pad tenancy that requires the park owner's consent; the assignment rules expressly recognise a park where every pad is reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 (or 2+ tenants, at least one of whom has reached 55), as set out in s. 10(2)(b)(i) of the Human Rights Code — the park owner can refuse an assignment where no purchaser meets that age requirement.

First Nations leased land adds a second layer at Cottonwood Village: the park is recorded as First Nations leased land, so the head lease (listing-stated expiry 2076 with an option to extend) sits above the pad tenancy — a buyer is reviewing the lease term and the park rules, not a strata Form B.

City zoning: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000: — in the AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone that frames the rural west, the minimum lot area is 7.5 ha for land excluded or exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within the ALR, 1 ha for a boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha for a homesite severance or boundary adjustment approved by the Agricultural Land Commission; minimum lot width is 25 m.

City plan: Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500: (adopted December 16, 2025) is the city-wide plan; the Agricultural Area Plan is its Schedule B1 and covers this area, and the OCP's housing policies support forming partnerships with senior levels of government and local sectors to deliver more affordable housing.

Flood rules: the City's Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 sets minimum building setbacks of 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal; the City maintains a diking network for the Fraser and Vedder River systems, and Chilliwack levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rates.

blocks.text: Good to know about West Chilliwack

items.t: The two Evans Road addresses side by side are opposite products: 7610 Evans Rd (Cottonwood Village) is 55+ leasehold park housing, and 7694 Evans Rd (Creekside Estates), a few doors from Evans Elementary, is a general-market strata with "no age restrictions" stated in its listings — search results that blur the corridor blur that distinction.

The lease clock is the real due-diligence item at Cottonwood: listings state a 2076 lease expiry with an option to extend on First Nations leased land — what a lender, an insurer and a future buyer will all ask about is the remaining term and the extension mechanics, so get the head-lease summary and park rules before subject removal.

"45+" and "40+" parks nearby are a different legal animal than they look: Country Park Village (45918 Knight Rd) is listed as 45+ and Rainbow Estates (9055 Ashwell Rd) as 40+ — in a strata those age numbers have been void since Nov 24, 2022, and in a park they survive only as park rules under the Human Rights Code 55+ framework's assignment rules, which are written around age 55. Read the actual park rules rather than the marketing number.

The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan (Schedule B5 of the 2050 OCP) expects the fastest growth in the seniors cohort city-wide — residents aged 75+ growing at 2.4% to 4.5% per year between 2016 and 2041 — which is the City's own context for why the Evans/Cottonwood corridor's seniors product is a park, not new strata construction.

Chilliwack taxes have two penalty steps and a dyking add-on: property tax notices are due the first working day after July 1 each year, with a 5% penalty on taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% on taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026, plus separate drainage and dyking levies on top of the municipal rates.

The City does not run any of the housing in its own inventory: the Chilliwack Housing Inventory 2026 states the City does not own, operate or manage any listed housing option and that inclusion does not imply endorsement or guaranteed availability — eligibility and availability always come from the operator.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ strata condo or townhome complex in West Chilliwack?
faq.a: No. No age-restricted strata or freehold ownership complex with a West Chilliwack address was verified in any source checked. The one strata building on Evans Road, Creekside Estates (7694 Evans Rd), is recorded as having "no age restrictions."

faq.q: What CAN a 55+ buyer actually buy on the Evans Road corridor?
faq.a: A manufactured home in Cottonwood Village (7610 Evans Rd) — a 55+ park of 143 units with a clubhouse, where you own the home, rent the pad, and the land is First Nations leased land with a listing-stated lease expiry of 2076 plus an option to extend. That is leasehold park tenure under the MHPTA, not strata or freehold ownership.

faq.q: Can the park refuse to let me buy because of age?
faq.a: In a 55+ park, yes, in effect: assignment of a pad tenancy needs the park owner's consent, and the provincial assignment rules recognise refusal where no purchaser meets the park's 55+ age requirement (Human Rights Code s. 10(2)(b)(i) framework). Get the park rules in writing before writing an offer — the seller must provide them.

faq.q: Are pets allowed at Cottonwood Village?
faq.a: The park specialist's list records 1 pet allowed at Cottonwood Village; an individual listing records 2 smaller pets permitted — the park rules govern, so confirm the current rule with the park before relying on either figure.

faq.q: Where are Chilliwack's 55+ strata buildings, then?
faq.a: Downtown and the central city: e.g. Ivy Green (45775 Spadina Ave, downtown — 55+, 24 condos, built 1994, LMS1336, no pets) and Knight Lodge (45660 Knight Rd — 55+ per listing restriction data).

faq.q: Where is the hospital and urgent care?
faq.a: Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Rd; the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is inside this corridor at #104 - 7955 Evans Road.

faq.q: Is there a bus on Evans Road?
faq.a: Yes — route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack via Evans Rd and Yale Rd, with timing points at Evans Rd at Yale Rd and Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd. Service levels/frequency: check the current BC Transit schedule before relying on it.

faq.q: What flood checks matter on a rural west-side lot?
faq.a: Measure the bylaw setbacks — 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River, 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal — and budget for the drainage and dyking levies the City adds on top of municipal tax rates.

faq.q: If I need subsidized seniors housing or care, where do I look?
faq.a: Not in this area: the BC Housing Zone 7 directory's Chilliwack seniors addresses are downtown/central (e.g. the Paramount, 46187 Yale Rd — 65+, income-tested, rent at 30% of income), and the registered assisted-living residences (Waverly Seniors Village, 8445 Young Rd; The Cascades, 45586 McIntosh Dr) are on the east/downtown side.
